lesson.title: Changing 2D List Rows
lesson.driving_question: How can familiar list operations add, place or remove complete rows?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Appending, inserting and deleting complete records
lesson.concept_budget: Reuse known 1D-list mutation operations with complete row values; no new mutation method is introduced.
misconceptions: A complete row is itself a list.
append() adds the row as one outer-list item.
insert() uses an outer-list row position.
del records[position] removes one complete row.
lesson.progression_note: Transfers established list-editing knowledge to complete 2D records before search is introduced.

shared_program.code:
clubs = [["Art", 12], ["Chess", 18]]
new_club = ["Code", 15]
clubs.append(new_club)
clubs.insert(1, ["Music", 9])
del clubs[0]
for club in clubs:
    print(club[0], club[1])

primm.prompt: Recall how append(), insert() and del change a 1D list. Treat each complete row as one outer-list item.
Trace the outer list after each of the three changes, then predict the three displayed records.
Run the supplied file and compare every intermediate row order with your trace.

questions: Why must a new record be added as one complete inner list rather than as separate outer-list items?
How do later row positions change after insert() adds a row at position 1?
What happens to the position of a row after an earlier row is deleted?
What three rows are printed after the append, insert and delete operations finish?

primm.prompt: Insert ["Drama", 11] at row position 0 and remove the deletion line. The final output must begin Drama 11.

Build an event schedule editor with three [event, room] rows. Insert one user-created row at a valid position, delete a different valid row from the enlarged schedule, and display numbered remaining rows using a counter.
Repair the appended row brackets and delete a complete row with an outer-list index.

programs.challenge2:
clubs = [["Art", 12], ["Chess", 18]]
name = input("New club: ")
members = int(input("Members: "))
new_club = [name, members]
clubs.append(new_club)
position = int(input("Delete row 0 to 2: "))
del clubs[position]
for club in clubs:
    print(club[0], club[1])
programs.challenge3:
schedule = [["Talk", 1], ["Quiz", 2], ["Demo", 3]]
position = int(input("Insert position 0 to 3: "))
event = input("Event: ")
room = int(input("Room: "))
schedule.insert(position, [event, room])
delete_position = int(input("Delete position 0 to 3: "))
del schedule[delete_position]
number = 0
for row in schedule:
    print(number, row[0], row[1])
    number = number + 1
